research_question: What is the effect of percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL, including mini-, super-mini, and micro-PCNL) compared with retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) on postoperative pain on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0) in adults with renal stones?
treatment_label: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL, including mini-, super-mini, and micro-PCNL)
outcome_description: Postoperative pain score on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0, first postoperative pain assessment within ~24 hours; earliest at or after 6 hours if multiple times reported, or 1-hour value if that is the only one available) measured on a 0–10 visual analogue scale (VAS).
positive_direction: Lower postoperative pain score with PCNL compared to RIRS (favours PCNL); under unadjusted raw difference (PCNL minus RIRS), MD > 0 indicates more pain after PCNL (favours RIRS)
search_queries: PCNL RIRS postoperative pain visual analogue scale trial
percutaneous nephrolithotomy retrograde intrarenal surgery pain randomized trial
PCNL versus RIRS kidney stones postoperative pain comparison
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing any form of percutaneous nephrolithotomy (standard PCNL, mini-PCNL, super-mini PCNL, or micro-PCNL) with retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS/flexible ureteroscopy) in adult patients with renal calculi
Reporting quantitative assessment of postoperative pain on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0 / within first 24 hours) on a visual analogue scale (VAS) or numerical rating scale
Reporting or allowing derivation of arm-level sample size, mean, and standard deviation (SD) for day-of-surgery pain
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, letters, comments, or conference abstracts without extractable data)
No comparative evaluation between PCNL (standard, mini, super-mini, or micro) and RIRS (e.g. single-arm studies, or comparisons solely against ESWL or open surgery)
No quantitative postoperative pain data on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0) convertible to mean and standard deviation per arm
Paediatric patient cohorts (under 18 years of age) or studies unrelated to surgical management of renal calculi
moderators_to_extract: PCNL technique and sheath size (standard PCNL vs mini-PCNL vs super-mini / micro-PCNL)
Mean stone size / burden (diameter in mm)
Postoperative pain assessment timing on day 0 (e.g. 1 hour, 6 hours, 12 hours)
Nephrostomy tube and ureteral stent placement strategy (e.g. tubeless vs stented vs nephrostomy)
Postoperative analgesia protocol or regional block administration
effect_size_note: Pool as a mean difference (MD) in points on a 0–10 VAS using a random-effects model. Extract mean, SD, and N for PCNL (treatment) and RIRS (control) arms for pain on postoperative day 0 (earliest assessment at or after 6 hours, or at 1 hour if only that is reported). If a 0–100 mm VAS is used, rescale to 0–10. Positive raw MD (PCNL - RIRS > 0) indicates more pain after PCNL (favors RIRS).
single_outcome_target: postoperative pain on day of surgery
